title: Original Luminary: bounded propulsion and inertial feedback
limitations: VERIFIED RECORDED AUTHENTIC AGC EXPERIMENT; playback is not live execution.
SYNTHETIC fixed-attitude fixture, not historical Apollo 11 flight data.
Original Luminary commands drive a simplified physical engine and navigation feedback.
RCS is disconnected; the crew accepted an attitude review without an achieved burn maneuver.
Engine response is instantaneous; inherited LM-7 parameters and nominal DECA gain are approximations.
Zero LOWCRIT/HIGHCRIT padloads and saturated thrust do not establish a calibrated throttle policy.
The recorded initial thrust is not established retrograde braking; no complete descent or landing is demonstrated.
Physical REF state and original stable-member navigation/PIPTIME are separate measurements.
Only actual observations are shown, held between samples without interpolation or extrapolation.

source.physicalSimulationEpoch: Raw time_s is elapsed model propagation from initialized mission-state epoch; replay t starts at physical fixture activation.
source.sampling: Actual physical observations, held; at most 0.25 s apart, no interpolation.
source.coordinateFrame: Moon-centered basic REF; original MUNRVG navigation uses stable-member coordinates.

navigation.sourceNote: AGC-computed navigation, separate from recorded physical REF state.

projection.downrange: reference radius times change in atan2(z,x), relative to first physical sample
projection.positivePitch: right-handed body +Y tilt from local radial up; thrust turns toward negative local XZ tangent
projection.caution: Local projections do not establish a historical trajectory or achieved burn attitude.
